raw_response:
I will keep my land mostly in the wheat-maize rotation, because in Quzhou this is the most reliable way for me to make a living. I know this system, I can manage it with ordinary machinery, and the weather, irrigation, and local grain market all fit it. I do not want to spread myself too thin with too many complicated crops. I will keep a small piece in peanut to leave myself one cash crop and reduce the risk of putting everything into grain. For wheat, I will hold the stand through spring with steady water and two key spray rounds, then harvest on time. Right after wheat harvest, I will seed summer maize quickly, keep fertilizer focused on yield, and use fewer tillage passes to save time and moisture. On peanut land, I will use cleaner field management and tighter pest watching, because if I let weeds and insects get ahead of me, the crop becomes troublesome fast. I am choosing simple, familiar, steady management over chasing the highest possible yield.
